title: The path is known by labor and generosity
subtitle: Raag Saarang
summary: The piece opens by exposing religious pose without wisdom, labor, or integrity behind it. It comes to a clean test: the one who works for what they eat and gives some away is the one who knows the path.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person confused by spiritual branding, costume, or authority language. Stayed with honestly, it returns discernment to labor, generosity, and humility.
takeaway: Honest labor and sharing reveal the path better than costume.

lines.translation: The one who lacks spiritual wisdom sings religious songs.
The hungry Mullah turns his home into a mosque.
The lazy unemployed has his ears pierced to look like a Yogi.
Someone else becomes a pan-handler, and loses his social status.
One who calls himself a guru or a spiritual teacher, while he goes around begging

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਾ ਕੈ ਮੂਲਿ ਨ ਲਗੀਐ ਪਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: taa kai mool na lageeaai pai ||

lines.translation: One who works for what he eats, and gives some of what he has
O Nanak, he knows the Path. ||1||

structure: The shabad begins by mocking hollow religious performances that substitute image for wisdom.
From there it refuses reverence toward the guru-figure who begs while claiming status.
The closing movement rests in a simple mark of truth: work honestly, give from your hands, and the path becomes recognizable.
